mainTopic: The ברכה over bread (המוציא) and whether cooked vegetables keep בורא פרי האדמה
overview: This amud begins by finishing the discussion of בר רב זביד, who said "מוציא" over bread to stay out of a מחלוקת. The הלכה is to say "המוציא", like the רבנן. The גמרא then turns to the משנה about vegetables. Because the משנה lists vegetables next to bread, אביי concludes that boiled vegetables (שלקות) still get בורא פרי האדמה. רב חסדא and רב נחמן report a dispute: רב and שמואל say בורא פרי האדמה, while עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן says שהכל. רב חסדא offers a middle view: cooking upgrades vegetables usually eaten cooked and downgrades ones like garlic and leeks. A link to a dispute among תנאים about cooked מצה is rejected. רב נחמן בר יצחק then shows that עולא relied on a weaker tradition, and רבי זירא supports this: רבי חייא בר אבא was the more careful student, and רבי יוחנן ruled בורא פרי האדמה on boiled lupin. A proof from a salted olive is pushed aside, and a challenge from מרור is answered. The amud ends as רבי ירמיה begins a question about the salted olive, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why did he say מוציא?
steps.stepSummary: Saying המוציא would have taught us something. Saying מוציא seems to teach nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If he had said "המוציא"] he would have taught us the meaning, and he would have taught us that the הלכה follows the רבנן. But since he said "מוציא", what is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking why בר רב זביד, who was praised as an expert in ברכות, chose the plain wording "מוציא", which everyone already accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי נחמיה and the רבנן argued whether "המוציא" can describe something done in the past. Saying "המוציא" would have shown that this expert sides with the רבנן. But "מוציא" is acceptable to everyone, so it seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason or meaning (here, how to read the word)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words "if he had said המוציא" (בשלמא אי אמר המוציא) come right before it on the daf.

phrases.english: he would have taught us the meaning,
and he would have taught us that the halakha follows the Rabbis.
But since he said "motzi",
what is he teaching us?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דַּאֲמַר ״מוֹצִיא״ מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question from the previous page about how בר רב זביד worded his ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An expert's choice of words should teach something. "מוציא" is agreed upon by all, so it teaches nothing.

steps.title: He wanted to stay out of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: He said מוציא on purpose, to use wording that everyone accepts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did this to keep himself out of the מחלוקת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he was not trying to teach anything. He simply chose wording that works according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that every word an expert chooses must teach a new idea. The answer is that sometimes the wise choice is to avoid taking sides. "מוציא" is valid for both רבי נחמיה and the רבנן.

phrases.english: He did this
to take himself out of the dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-explains his motive: he was avoiding a side, not teaching a new idea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed his wording must teach something new.
steps.terutzMaskana: He chose wording that is valid according to all opinions.

steps.title: The הלכה: say המוציא
steps.stepSummary: The final ruling is to say "המוציא לחם מן הארץ", following the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is to say "המוציא לחם מן הארץ", because we rule like the רבנן, who say that "המוציא" also means "brought out" in the past.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling for the ברכה over bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה worried that "המוציא" refers only to the past, so he said "מוציא". The רבנן hold that "המוציא" also fits a past action, so it is a proper ברכה. We follow the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: "Who brings forth bread from the earth", the ברכה over bread
since we hold (as an established rule)

steps.whatToRemember: The practical הלכה is to say "המוציא", like the רבנן. Saying "מוציא" is valid according to everyone, but it is not the standard wording.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the ברכה over bread is said today as "המוציא לחם מן הארץ".

phrases.english: And the halakha is: "Who brings forth bread from the earth,"
since we hold like the Rabbis,
who say that it also means "brought forth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the המוציא discussion with a practical ruling.

steps.title: Vegetables are compared to bread
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists vegetables next to bread. So vegetables, like bread, keep their ברכה after being changed by fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "And over vegetables one says..." It teaches vegetables as similar to bread. Just as bread is something changed by fire, vegetables too are being discussed after they were changed by fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about vegetables, and draws a comparison to bread. This sets up the rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat turns into bread by baking, and it still gets a special ברכה. Because the משנה places vegetables right next to bread, the גמרא reads it as saying that cooked vegetables also keep their normal ברכה.

phrases.english: "And over vegetables one says," etc.
It teaches vegetables as similar to bread:

phrases.aramaic: מָה פַּת שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנָּה עַל יְדֵי הָאוּר,
phrases.english: just as bread was changed by fire,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יְרָקוֹת נָמֵי שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנּוּ עַל יְדֵי הָאוּר.
phrases.english: so too vegetables that were changed by fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's vegetables include cooked ones, just as bread is a cooked food.

steps.title: אביי: boiled vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה
steps.stepSummary: רבנאי, quoting אביי, says the comparison to bread proves that boiled vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנאי said in the name of אביי: This means that over boiled vegetables we say "בורא פרי האדמה". From where do we know this? From the fact that the משנה teaches vegetables as similar to bread.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא turns the comparison from step 4 into a clear practical rule and points to its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed the comparison. Here it becomes a rule: cooking does not downgrade a vegetable's ברכה. The question "ממאי" just points back to the comparison to bread.

keyTerms.meaning: this means; a practical rule drawn from a source
the ברכה over produce that grows from the ground

phrases.english: Rabbenai said in the name of Abaye:
This means
that over boiled vegetables one recites "Who creates fruit of the ground."
From where?
From the fact that it teaches vegetables as similar to bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the comparison in step 4 into a practical rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Boiled vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה.

steps.title: רב: boiled vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא publicly taught, in the name of רב, that boiled vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא taught publicly in the name of "רבינו" (and who is that? רב): over boiled vegetables we say "בורא פרי האדמה".
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא begins reporting a מחלוקת. This first view, from רב, agrees with אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The title "רבינו" (our teacher) refers to רב. His view matches the inference from the משנה: cooking keeps the vegetable's ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: "our teacher", a title here meaning רב

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda taught in the name of Rabbeinu,
and who is he? Rav:
over boiled vegetables one recites "Who creates fruit of the ground."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an אמורא who agrees with the rule in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, boiled vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: boiled vegetables get שהכל
steps.stepSummary: עולא, quoting רבי יוחנן, holds the opposite: boiled vegetables get שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our teachers who came down from ארץ ישראל (and who is that? עולא, in the name of רבי יוחנן) said: over boiled vegetables we say "שהכל נהיה בדברו".
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא now gives the opposing view, which came from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that boiling changes a vegetable so much that it loses its "fruit of the ground" status. So it gets the general ברכה of שהכל. This directly argues with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: those who came down from ארץ ישראל to בבל
the general ברכה, "by whose word all things came to be"

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's view does not mean the vegetable stops being a vegetable. It means the specific ברכה changes after cooking.

phrases.english: And our Rabbis who came down from Eretz Yisrael,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַנּוּ — עוּלָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר:
phrases.english: and who is that? Ulla, in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan, said:
over boiled vegetables one recites "By whose word all things came to be."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to רב's in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, boiled vegetables get שהכל.

steps.title: רב חסדא's middle view
steps.stepSummary: It depends on the vegetable. If it is normally eaten raw, cooking downgrades it to שהכל. If it is normally eaten cooked, cooking upgrades it to בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say: anything that raw gets "בורא פרי האדמה", once boiled gets "שהכל". And anything that raw gets "שהכל", once boiled gets "בורא פרי האדמה".
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives his own view, which divides vegetables into two groups based on their normal way of being eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה follows the vegetable's best, normal state. If a vegetable is good raw, boiling spoils it, so it drops to שהכל. If a vegetable is not normally eaten raw, it only gets שהכל raw, and cooking brings it to its proper state, so it gets בורא פרי האדמה.

keyTerms.meaning: and I say (the speaker's own view)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on boiled vegetables. רב: בורא פרי האדמה. רבי יוחנן: שהכל. רב חסדא: it depends on whether the vegetable is normally eaten raw or cooked.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a food's ברכה follows the way it is normally eaten becomes a basic principle in הלכות ברכות.

phrases.english: And I say:
anything whose original (raw) blessing is "Who creates fruit of the ground,"
if he boiled it: "By whose word all things came to be."
And anything whose original (raw) blessing is "By whose word all things came to be,"
if he boiled it: "Who creates fruit of the ground."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁתְּחִלָּתוֹ ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a middle position between רב (step 6) and רבי יוחנן (step 7).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooking reverses the ברכה: raw-eaten vegetables become שהכל, and cooked-eaten vegetables become בורא פרי האדמה.

steps.title: Where do we find a vegetable that cooking downgrades?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that some vegetables are upgraded by cooking, such as cabbage, chard and pumpkin. It then asks for a real example of a vegetable that is downgraded by cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, a vegetable whose raw ברכה is שהכל and whose cooked ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה is easy to find: cabbage, chard and pumpkin. But a vegetable whose raw ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה and whose cooked ברכה is שהכל, how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the two-sided rule from Step 8. It asks for an actual example of the 'downgrade' side. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'upgrade' side is easy to picture. Cabbage, chard and pumpkin are hard to eat raw, and cooking makes them good. The 'downgrade' side is harder to picture, since cooking usually improves food. So the גמרא wants to know whether such a case really exists.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part is fine (it introduces the side that is not a problem)
How would you find such a case?

phrases.english: Granted, anything whose original (raw) blessing is
phrases.notes: בשלמא marks the easy half before the difficult half.

phrases.english: "By whose word all things came to be"
when he boiled it, "Who creates fruit of the ground"
you can find it with cabbage, chard, and pumpkin;
phrases.notes: These are hardly edible raw, so cooking upgrades them.

phrases.english: but anything whose original blessing is "Who creates fruit of the ground"
and when he boiled it, "By whose word all things",
how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a concrete example of the downgrade half of the rule in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real vegetable that gets בורא פרי האדמה raw but only שהכל once cooked.

steps.title: Garlic and leeks are the downgrade case
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that garlic and leeks are examples: their ברכה drops when they are cooked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: You can find it with garlic and leeks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the example the גמרא asked for. Garlic and leeks are normally eaten raw, and cooking spoils them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Garlic and leeks are valued for their sharp taste when raw. Cooking weakens that taste, so the cooked version is a worse form of the food. This shows the downgrade half of Step 8 is real and not just theory.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
You can find it with garlic and leeks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Garlic and leeks: their ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה raw and שהכל when cooked.

steps.title: רב נחמן reports both sides of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן teaches that שמואל holds cooked vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה. He then reports that עולא, in the name of רבי יוחנן, holds they get שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן taught in the name of 'our teacher', meaning שמואל: on cooked vegetables we say בורא פרי האדמה. And 'our colleagues who came down from ארץ ישראל', meaning עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן, said: on cooked vegetables we say שהכל נהיה בדברו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another report of the same disagreement about cooked vegetables. This time רב נחמן presents both sides. This sets up his own comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב חסדא taught the lenient view in the name of רב. Now רב נחמן teaches the same view in the name of שמואל. So both great Babylonian teachers hold בורא פרי האדמה. Against them stands עולא, quoting רבי יוחנן from ארץ ישראל, who holds שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: Our colleagues who came down from ארץ ישראל (here, עולא)

steps.confusionAlert: This is רב נחמן, not רב נחמן בר יצחק from the step before. These are two different אמוראים.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman taught in the name of "our teacher,"
and who is that? Shmuel:
phrases.notes: The גמרא explains who the title refers to.

phrases.english: Over boiled vegetables one recites "Who creates fruit of the ground."
And our colleagues who came down from Eretz Yisrael,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַנּוּ — עוּלָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר:
phrases.english: and who is that? Ulla, in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan, said:
Over boiled vegetables one recites "By whose word all things came to be."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ, וּמַנּוּ — שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the dispute of Steps 6-7 with a new chain of tradition: שמואל vs. עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: cooked vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה. עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן: cooked vegetables get שהכל.

steps.title: רב נחמן links the dispute to a debate about cooked מצה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן suggests that this disagreement is really an older dispute among תנאים. רבי מאיר holds one can fulfill the מצוה with cooked מצה. רבי יוסי holds one cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say this is a dispute already taught among תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: one fulfills the מצוה of מצה with a soaked wafer, and with a cooked one as long as it did not fall apart. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: one fulfills it with a soaked wafer, but not with a cooked one, even if it did not fall apart.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers a source showing that the אמוראים are repeating an older debate. Cooking either spoils food or it does not, and the תנאים already disagreed about that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that cooked מצה is still good מצה, so cooking does not spoil food. He would match שמואל's בורא פרי האדמה. רבי יוסי holds that cooked מצה no longer counts, so cooking spoils food. He would match רבי יוחנן's שהכל.

phrases.english: And I say it is taught as a dispute.
phrases.notes: רב נחמן speaking: the אמוראים follow two sides of a debate among תנאים.

phrases.english: As it was taught: one fulfills (the מצוה of matza) with a soaked wafer
and with a boiled one that did not dissolve —
the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: יוֹצְאִים בְּרָקִיק הַשָּׁרוּי,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei says: one fulfills it with a soaked wafer,
but not with a boiled one,
even if it did not dissolve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן ties the two positions he just reported to a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute between שמואל and רבי יוחנן about cooked vegetables is already a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about cooked מצה: רבי מאיר says it is valid, רבי יוסי says it is not.

steps.title: The מצה link is rejected; everyone agrees cooked vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב נחמן's link. רבי יוסי invalidates cooked מצה only because the מצוה needs the taste of מצה. For the ברכה on vegetables, even רבי יוסי agrees the answer is בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not so. Everyone agrees that cooked vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה. רבי יוסי only said his ruling there because we need the taste of מצה, and it is missing. But here, even רבי יוסי agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's comparison. It shows that the מצה case works for its own special reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצה case does not test whether cooking spoils food in general. It tests whether the specific taste of מצה, which the מצוה requires, survives cooking. Cooking can change that taste and still leave a vegetable as a perfectly good vegetable. So רבי יוסי's ruling says nothing about the ברכה on vegetables.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his ruling (in that specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: There is no dispute among תנאים here. רבי יוסי's ruling on cooked מצה is a special rule for the מצוה of מצה, which needs the taste of מצה. The גמרא says everyone agrees cooked vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה. It does not address the garlic-and-leeks exception from the earlier steps.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a common method in the גמרא. A ruling given in one area, such as a מצוה with its own requirements, should not be stretched into a general rule for another area, such as ברכות.

phrases.english: But that is not so,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא שְׁלָקוֹת מְבָרְכִין עֲלֵיהֶן ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה״,
phrases.english: for everyone agrees that over boiled vegetables one recites "Who creates fruit of the ground,"

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei only said his ruling there
because we require the taste of matza,
and it is not there;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מוֹדֶה.
phrases.english: but here, even Rabbi Yosei agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב נחמן's attempt in Step 12 to tie the dispute to the תנאים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the link between the vegetable dispute and the cooked-מצה dispute. It also claims everyone agrees that cooked vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מצה ruling depends on a requirement special to the מצוה (the taste of מצה). It is not a general rule that cooking spoils food.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Cooked vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה according to everyone, and רבי יוסי agrees in this case.

steps.title: Two students report different rulings from רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן as saying בורא פרי האדמה on שלקות. רבי בנימין בר יפת quotes רבי יוחנן as saying שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: over cooked vegetables we say 'בורא פרי האדמה'. רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי יוחנן: over cooked vegetables we say 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents two opposite quotes from the same teacher, רבי יוחנן, about the ברכה on cooked vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, עולא quoted רבי יוחנן as holding שהכל. Now we learn that this was not the only version. There is a competing report that רבי יוחנן said בורא פרי האדמה, so the question becomes which student quoted him correctly.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה on produce that grows from the ground
The general ברכה: 'by whose word all things came to be'
We recite a ברכה over them

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Over cooked vegetables, one recites
'Who creates fruit of the ground,'

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Over cooked vegetables, one recites
'By whose word all things came to be.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to עולא's quote of רבי יוחנן from step 11 and shows that there are two conflicting versions of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two traditions of רבי יוחנן's view on שלקות: בורא פרי האדמה (רבי חייא בר אבא) and שהכל (רבי בנימין בר יפת).

steps.title: עולא followed the wrong version
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that עולא locked in a mistake by following רבי בנימין בר יפת's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: עולא made his mistake permanent by following רבי בנימין בר יפת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains where עולא's שהכל ruling came from. He calls it an error.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's view (step 11) was based on רבי בנימין בר יפת's report. רב נחמן בר יצחק calls it a שיבוש, a mistake. This sets up the next steps, which explain why that report is less reliable.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who quoted רבי יוחנן as holding שהכל

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this רב נחמן בר יצחק with רב נחמן from step 11. Here רב נחמן בר יצחק is criticizing עולא's source. He is not agreeing with it.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Ulla established his error
in accordance with Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies עולא's ruling with the second of the two traditions and labels it a mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא's שהכל view comes from רבי בנימין בר יפת's report, and it is mistaken.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא was the more careful student
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks how רבי בנימין בר יפת can even be compared to רבי חייא בר אבא. He gives two reasons: רבי חייא בר אבא was precise, and he reviewed his learning with רבי יוחנן every thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא wondered: How can רבי בנימין בר יפת be put next to רבי חייא בר אבא? רבי חייא בר אבא was careful and learned the teaching precisely from his teacher, רבי יוחנן. רבי בנימין בר יפת was not careful. Also, every thirty days רבי חייא בר אבא reviewed his learning in front of רבי יוחנן. רבי בנימין בר יפת did not review.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges relying on רבי בנימין בר יפת at all. He argues that רבי חייא בר אבא's report is far more trustworthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attack is not about logic. It is about the reliability of the person passing on the teaching. רבי חייא בר אבא was precise, and he regularly checked his learning with רבי יוחנן himself. So when the two reports conflict, his version wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Wondered about it, was puzzled by it

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira wondered about it:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיָן רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת
phrases.english: What does Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet have to do
next to Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba?
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba was precise
and learned the teaching from Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת לָא דָּיֵיק.
phrases.english: while Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet was not precise.
Furthermore, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba,
every thirty days,

phrases.aramaic: מַהְדַּר תַּלְמוּדֵיהּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: reviews his learning before Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת לָא מַהְדַּר.
phrases.english: while Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet does not review.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and strengthens the claim that עולא's source was unreliable by comparing the two reporters.
steps.kashyaTarget: Relying on רבי בנימין בר יפת's version of רבי יוחנן (and so עולא's ruling)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When two students conflict, follow the more precise one who regularly reviewed with the teacher. That is רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא בר אבא's version (רבי יוחנן: שלקות get בורא פרי האדמה) is correct, and עולא's שהכל tradition is a mistake.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The comparison between the two reporters: רבי חייא בר אבא was precise and reviewed his learning with רבי יוחנן every thirty days, while רבי בנימין בר יפת did neither.

steps.title: The boiled lupin story
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was asked about תורמוס that is boiled seven times and eaten as dessert. He ruled בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides all this: there was lupin that people boiled seven times in a pot and ate at the end of the meal. They came and asked רבי יוחנן, and he told them: over it we say 'בורא פרי האדמה'.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing his argument, רבי זירא adds a real case where רבי יוחנן himself ruled בורא פרי האדמה on a heavily cooked vegetable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a vegetable cooked seven times still got בורא פרי האדמה from רבי יוחנן. This directly supports רבי חייא בר אבא's report that רבי יוחנן holds שלקות keep their original ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Lupin, a bitter bean that needs heavy boiling
Dessert, the end of the meal

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, בַּר מִן דֵּין וּבַר מִן דֵּין,
phrases.english: Furthermore, besides this and besides that,
there was that lupin
which they boil seven times in a pot
and eat it as dessert at the end of a meal;
they came and asked Rabbi Yochanan,
and he said to them:
One recites over it 'Who creates fruit of the ground.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, בַּר מִן דֵּין וּבַר מִן דֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a factual proof from רבי יוחנן's own ruling on top of the argument about which student was more reliable.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן holds שלקות get בורא פרי האדמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling on boiled תורמוס

steps.title: The salted olive proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא saw רבי יוחנן bless before and after eating a salted olive. That makes sense if cooked food keeps its status, since the ברכה after would be מעין שלש. If it became שהכל, what ברכה would he say afterward?
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, רבי חייא בר אבא said: I saw רבי יוחנן eat a salted olive, and he made a ברכה on it before and after. If you say cooked foods keep their status, that works: first he says 'בורא פרי העץ', and afterward he says the ברכה אחת מעין שלש. But if you say cooked foods lose their status, then at the start he says 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'. But afterward, what ברכה would he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof from רבי יוחנן's behavior. A salted olive counts like cooked food, and he made a ברכה both before and after eating it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A salted (pickled) olive is treated like a cooked food. If cooking does not change its status, it is still one of the שבעת המינים: בורא פרי העץ before and ברכה מעין שלש after. If it had become שהכל, the גמרא assumes there would be no clear ברכה to say afterward. So the ברכה אחרונה that רבי יוחנן said shows the olive kept its status.

keyTerms.meaning: A salted (pickled) olive, treated like cooked food
They remain in their original state
The single after-blessing that summarizes the three ברכות of ברכת המזון
The ברכה on fruit of a tree

steps.confusionAlert: The olive was not boiled. It was salted. The proof works only because salting is treated like cooking, so it tests the same question as שלקות.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Furthermore, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:
I saw Rabbi Yochanan
eat a salted olive,
and he blessed over it before and after.
Granted, if you say
cooked foods remain in their original state,
at the start he recites over it 'Who creates fruit of the tree,'
and at the end he recites over it
one blessing summarizing the three.
But if you say
cooked foods do not remain in their original state,
granted, at the start he recites over it
'By whose word all things came to be,'
but at the end, what does he recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof from רבי יוחנן's behavior, this time built on the ברכה אחרונה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן holds שלקות keep their original ברכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר אבא's eyewitness account of רבי יוחנן blessing before and after a salted olive

steps.title: Perhaps he said בורא נפשות afterward
steps.stepSummary: The olive proof is pushed aside. Even if the olive became שהכל, רבי יוחנן could have said בורא נפשות afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he said afterward: 'בורא נפשות רבות וחסרונן על כל מה שברא' (Who creates many living beings and their needs, for all that He created).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the salted olive proof by showing there is a possible ברכה אחרונה even for a שהכל food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that a שהכל food has no ברכה אחרונה. The גמרא answers that בורא נפשות could serve as the after-blessing. So seeing רבי יוחנן bless afterward does not prove that the olive kept its status. Only this one proof falls. The reliability argument and the lupin proof still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The general after-blessing: 'Who creates many living beings'

steps.whatToRemember: The accepted tradition is that רבי יוחנן held שלקות get בורא פרי האדמה. Two things support it: רבי חייא בר אבא was the more reliable student, and רבי יוחנן ruled that way on the boiled תורמוס. The salted olive proof is rejected, because בורא נפשות could have been the after-blessing.

phrases.english: Perhaps: 'Who creates many living beings and their needs,
for all that He created.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the salted olive proof from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the salted olive proof. The earlier proofs are not affected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed that a שהכל food has no ברכה אחרונה. In fact, בורא נפשות could serve that role.

steps.title: A challenge from the laws of מרור on פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר שמואל brings a ברייתא: you cannot fulfill מרור with pickled, שלוקין, or cooked vegetables. If cooking does not change a vegetable's status, why are boiled vegetables not allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל raised an objection: 'The vegetables you can use for your obligation on פסח: you can use them and their stalks, but not pickled, not boiled, and not cooked.' If you think cooked vegetables keep their original status, why aren't boiled ones allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view that cooked vegetables keep their original status and ברכה. It uses a ברייתא about מרור on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view under attack is that cooked vegetables stay 'the same food' and keep the ברכה of בורא פרי האדמה. The ברייתא says boiled vegetables do not count for מרור. That seems to show that boiling changes what the vegetable is.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from an earlier source like a משנה or ברייתא
His obligation, meaning fulfilling a מצוה
Stalk or stem of a vegetable
Pickled, soaked in liquid for a long time
They remain in their original state

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about the מצוה of מרור, not about ברכות. The challenge works only by comparison: if boiling does not change the vegetable for ברכות, why does it change it for מרור?

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel raised an objection:
Vegetables with which a person fulfills
his obligation on Passover —
he fulfills it with them and with their stalks,
but not with pickled ones,
phrases.notes: Pickled means soaked a long time in liquid.

phrases.english: and not boiled ones, and not cooked ones.
And if it enters your mind
that they remain in their original state —
why are boiled ones not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the olive proof was pushed aside in Step 19, the גמרא brings a new source against the view that cooked food keeps its original status.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view, reported by רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן, that cooked vegetables keep their original status and ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If boiling does not change a vegetable, boiled vegetables should still count for מרור. The ברייתא says they do not, so boiling seems to change the vegetable.

steps.title: מרור needs a bitter taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מרור is a special case. The מצוה needs the bitter taste of מרור, and boiling removes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because we need the taste of מרור, and it is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the מרור case has its own special requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boiling can leave the vegetable the same food for ברכות and still ruin it for מרור. מרור requires a bitter taste, and boiled vegetables lose it. So the ברייתא is about taste, not about whether the vegetable changed its basic identity.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; the case in that source is special
It is not there; it is missing

steps.whyThisMatters: Losing one quality, like taste, does not mean a food lost its basic identity. A food can stay the same for ברכות and still fail a מצוה that needs a specific feature.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because we require the taste of bitter herbs, and it is missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (שאני התם): the source has its own special requirement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought that boiled vegetables fail for מרור because boiling changed what the vegetable is.
steps.terutzMaskana: They fail only because מרור needs a bitter taste, which boiling removes. Their basic status can stay the same.

steps.title: How did רבי יוחנן bless on a salted olive?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא how רבי יוחנן could say a ברכה over a salted olive, since its pit was removed. The question finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: How did רבי יוחנן say a ברכה over a salted olive? Since its pit was removed…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of רבי יוחנן and the salted olive from Step 18 and starts a new question about it. This step is only the setup, and the question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said רבי יוחנן made a ברכה before and after eating a salted olive. רבי ירמיה points out that the pit was taken out, so less food was actually eaten. This sets up a problem with the ברכה after eating, which needs a minimum amount.

keyTerms.meaning: How could he make a ברכה?
Pit or seed of a fruit

steps.confusionAlert: This passage ends in the middle of רבי ירמיה's question. Do not try to finish it here; the rest comes on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
How did Rabbi Yochanan make a blessing
over a salted olive?
Since its pit was removed
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מרור discussion and goes back to the salted olive story from Step 18 to raise a new difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report in Step 18 that רבי יוחנן made a ברכה after eating a salted olive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With the pit removed, the olive may be too small to require a ברכה after eating. The full argument is completed on the next amud.
